bib.title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses. Lin J., Liu S., Pan C., Lin L., Dou S., Xi Z., Huang X., Yan H., Han Z., Gui T., Jiang Y.-G. (Fudan, Peking, Shanghai Qiji Zhifeng). Preprint, arXiv:2604.25850v4, 18 May 2026.

COVERAGE: 128,455 of 128,455 chars, all 35 pages. References were skimmed for origins. Nothing was skipped. Quotes join line breaks with a space and otherwise keep the extraction's spacing.

NOTE FIT: 08-maturity-and-failure-modes.md is the best primary home.
- It sits under Open frontiers #2 ("Agents analyzing their own traces... automating the ratchet"), next to the Object-Oriented Harness section.
- It also bears on the "Self-improvers" branch and Stage 4. That branch is described as modifying prompts, while AHE edits tools, middleware and memory too, and prompt-only edits regressed.
- The Table 3 ablation is a useful secondary citation for 02-harness-anatomy.md.
- The publish-guard case study (p28-34) fits 04-execution-boundaries.md#prompts-vs-hooks. Attribution and proxy validation fit 05-verification-loops.md#trace-driven-improvement. I saw these anchors linked from note 08 but did not read those two notes.

CLAIMS
- claim: Ten automatic iterations raised pass@1 from a bash-only seed past all baselines overall.
  number: 69.7% to 77.0% (Codex 71.9, TF-GRPO 72.3, ACE 68.9, Terminus-2 62.9, OpenCode 47.2)
  setup: Terminal-Bench 2, 89 tasks (4 easy, 55 medium, 30 hard), GPT-5.4 high, 1-hour per-task timeout, k=2 rollouts in the reference run, one campaign of about 32 hours. Timeouts and infrastructure aborts count as failures.
  quote: "ten AHE iterations lift pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 from 69.7% to 77.0%, surpassing the human-designed harness Codex (71.9%)"; "We run a single AHE campaign of ten itera- tions"
  where: p1, p6 Table 1
- claim: Codex stays ahead on the Hard tier.
  number: Hard: AHE 53.3%, Codex 56.7%, seed 51.7%
  setup: same, 30 Hard tasks
  quote: "AHE 77.0% 100.0% 88.2%53.3%"; "Codex 71.9% 75.0% 80.0%56.7%"; "the only exception is the Hard tier, where AHE marginally trails Codex"
  where: p6
- claim: Isolated components carry the gain, while the system prompt alone regresses below the seed.
  number: memory only 75.3%, tool only 73.0%, middleware only 71.9%, prompt only 67.4%, seed 69.7%, full 77.0%
  setup: each AHE component is swapped alone into the seed; Terminal-Bench 2, 89 tasks
  quote: "+ memory only 75.3% 50.0% 83.6%63.3%"; "+ system_prompt only 67.4% 75.0% 78.2% 46.7%"
  where: p8 Table 3
- claim: Components interact non-additively, so stacking caps the gain; the authors attribute this to redundant closure checks using up long-horizon turns.
  number: +11.1 pp summed singles vs +7.3 pp full; Hard: memory only 63.3% vs full 53.3%
  setup: Table 3
  quote: "The three positive single- component gains sum to +11.1 pp against full AHE's +7.3 pp"
  where: p9
- claim: One component can help one tier and hurt another: memory only lifts Hard but drops Easy.
  number: Easy 50.0% vs seed 87.5%; Hard 63.3% vs seed 51.7%
  setup: 4 Easy and 30 Hard tasks
  quote: "+ memory only 75.3% 50.0% 83.6%63.3%"; "NexAU0 69.7% 87.5% 78.2% 51.7%"
  where: p8
- claim: The evolver predicts fixes far better than chance but barely foresees regressions.
  number: fix P 33.7% / R 51.4% vs random 6.5% / 10.6%; regression P 11.8% / R 11.1% vs random 5.6% / 5.4%
  setup: cross-iteration means over 9 evaluation rounds, computed over the 89 tasks, GPT-5.4 loop
  quote: "fix-precision of33.7%and fix-recall of 51.4%sit roughly 5x above the random-prediction baselines of 6.5% and 10.6%"; "regression- precision of11.8%and regression-recall of11.1%sit only about 2x above their random baselines of 5.6% and 5.4%"
  where: p9
- claim: Cumulatively, few regression predictions landed and most actual regressions went unforeseen.
  number: 43 predicted, 5 landed, P=11.6%; 40 unforeseen, R=11.1%
  setup: 9 rounds
  quote: "the agent issued 43 unique regression predictions and only 5 landed, giving cumulative P= 11.6% , while 40 regressions the agent did not foresee actually occurred"
  where: p35
- claim: On SWE-bench-verified the frozen harness has the highest aggregate success among the seed and self-evolved loops, and the lowest token use.
  number: 75.6% (seed 75.2, ACE 74.6, TF-GRPO 74.2); 461k tokens (seed 526, TF-GRPO 582, ACE 679), which is 12% below the seed
  setup: 500 tasks, 7 repos, GPT-5.4, no re-evolution. Aborted and timed-out trials are excluded from token means. No human-designed harness is in this table.
  quote: "All 500 74.6% 74.2% 75.2%75.6%679 582 526461"; "AHE also cuts aggregate tokens by 32% against ACE, 21% against TF-GRPO, and 12% against the seed"
  where: p7 Table 2
- claim: AHE falls below the seed on the three smallest repos; the authors call these marginal and attribute them to variance.
  number: scikit-learn 87.5 vs 93.8; pydata 72.7 vs 77.3; astropy 50.0 vs 54.5
  setup: n=32, 22, 22
  quote: "scikit-learn 3293.8% 93.8% 93.8%87.5%"; "Marginal regressions appear only on the three smallest repositories"
  where: p7
- claim: Prompt-only baselines cost more and regress off-target.
  number: 11% to 29% more tokens than the seed, with lower success
  setup: ACE and TF-GRPO evolved on Terminal-Bench 2, tested on SWE-bench-verified
  quote: "ACE and TF-GRPO both regress below the NexAU0 seed in aggregate success while spending 11% to 29% more tokens than the seed"
  where: p7
- claim: The evolved harness gains on every alternate model base, and the largest gains are on other families.
  number: deepseek-v4-flash 51.7 to 61.8 (+10.1); qwen-3.6-plus 56.2 to 62.5 (+6.3); gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview 36.5 to 41.6 (+5.1); GPT-5.4 medium 65.7 to 68.0 (+2.3); GPT-5.4 xhigh 72.5 to 74.7 (printed +2.3)
  setup: Terminal-Bench 2, 89 tasks, each base paired with the seed on that same base, no re-evolution
  quote: "deepseek-v4-flash moves +10.1 pp from 51.7% to 61.8%, qwen-3.6-plus +6.3 pp from 56.2% to 62.5%, and gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview +5.1 pp from 36.5% to 41.6%, all above the +2.3 pp on GPT-5.4 medium and xhigh"
  where: p7, p8 Fig 3
- claim: Evidence compression and the edit contract are the mechanism; the seed is deliberately minimal so that every added component is attributable. The evolver writes only in the workspace; tracer, verifier and LLM config are read-only.
  number: ~10M raw trace tokens to ~10K overview; 7 component types
  setup: figure label; NexAU framework
  quote: "~10M tokens ~10K tokens Overview"; "exposes seven orthogonal component types as explicit files"
  where: p4
- claim: A stated rule did not stop a repeated failure until the tool enforced it. On path-tracing the agent deleted its verified output during cleanup; a shell guard flipped the task, and an override token later became a loophole that was hardened to a hard block at iteration 8.
  number: 0/2 to 2/2 (path-tracing, iteration 5); 0/2 to 2/2 (configure-git-webserver, iteration 8)
  setup: single-task case studies, k=2
  quote: "The seed harness's prompt advice against "destroying verified state" was already present, but no execution-time mechanism enforced it. At iteration 5 path-tracing flips from 0/2 to 2/2."
  where: p28; override loophole p30-31
- claim: Warnings appended to tool output were ignored on the next turn; moving them into the next model turn fixed four tasks. This was part of the biggest single jump of the run, to its high-water mark.
  number: 76.97 at iteration 8, after a dip from 75.8 to 73.0
  setup: iteration 8, Terminal-Bench 2
  quote: "Iteration 8's overall score lands at 76.97, the run's high-water mark"; "the score had regressed from 75.8 to 73.0"
  where: p30-31
- claim: The recurring failure was proxy validation: closing on row counts or file existence rather than the evaluator's assertions. An edit can also fix a task it never predicted.
  number: none
  setup: db-wal-recovery, seed vs iteration 2
  quote: "proxy validation instead of evaluator-isomorphic validation"; "predicted_fixes field for chg-1 did not list db-wal-recovery"
  where: p27
- claim: Authors' labels for the transfer results: gains come from "general engineering experience", and factual harness structure transfers while prose strategy does not. These are interpretations, not tested separately.
  number: none
  setup: Tables 2-3, Fig 3
  quote: "factual harness structure transfers across tasks and models whereas prose-level strategy does not"
  where: p2

LIMITS
Conceded by the authors (p9-10):
- Other languages, repo-scale deployment and human-in-the-loop workflows are untested.
- The step budget and timeout were fitted to GPT-5.4 high, so transfer figures "conflate harness portability with operating-point coupling".
- It is "a controlled research prototype", with long-horizon cleanup and misuse prevention incomplete.
- Interaction-aware evolution and regression foresight are left to future work.

Not shown, from my reading:
- There are no confidence intervals or significance tests, and only one campaign, so run-to-run variance is unknown.
- There is no held-out split on Terminal-Bench 2. H_best is selected by pass@1 on the same 89 tasks (Algorithm 1, line 14), so 77.0% is an in-sample best of ten. No separate re-evaluation is described.
- The evolve prompt forbids task-specific logic and reverse-engineering tests, but no check of compliance is reported. Task names do appear in manifests.
- The ablation is add-one only, on four of seven component types. There is no leave-one-out, and skills and sub-agents are not isolated.
- SWE-bench has no Codex or other human-designed harness, so "highest aggregate" is only against the seed and self-evolved loops. It is a 0.4 pp margin.
- Terminal-Bench token figures are absent from Tables 1 and 3, even though two metrics are promised. The token claim rests on SWE-bench only, and the token cost of evolution itself is not reported (only about 32 hours).
- No rollback counts are given. Fig 8 describes automatic rollback, while the evolve prompt leaves KEEP/IMPROVE/ROLLBACK to the agent, and at iteration 7 it chose not to roll back.
- The method for the random-prediction baseline is not described.
- The alternate bases are budget tiers (flash, flash-lite) plus qwen, and no Claude model is tested. The saturation explanation is not tested.
- "Minimal human prior" (p3) needs qualifying. The explore agent's prompt seeds web searches for "pre-completion verification middleware", "doom loop detection" and a "tool_impl > middleware > tool_desc > skill > system_prompt" hierarchy (p25-26), so some of what AHE "discovers" was pointed to.
- Dated: GPT-5.4-era models and May 2026 baselines.

My arithmetic, not in the paper:
- Printed percentages fit k=2 for seed, AHE and ablations. AHE is 137/178 and the seed 124/178, so the +7.3 pp gain is 13 rollouts.
- They fit k=1 for the human harnesses (Codex 64/89) and k=3 for ACE and TF-GRPO (e.g. 91.7% Easy = 11/12). If so, the comparison panel used unequal rollouts. The paper says "each table states it explicitly" (p15), but the tables as extracted do not.
- The SWE-bench margin fits 378 vs 376 of 500 tasks, assuming k=1.
- Each small-repo regression is about 1 to 2 tasks.

CODE:
Change-manifest entry, p20-21 (Appendix B.2), with the page-number line removed:
```json
{
"id": "chg-1",
"type": "new|improvement|rollback",
"description": "What was changed and why",
"files": ["relative/to/workspace/file.py"],
"failure_pattern": "The failure class this addresses",
"predicted_fixes": ["task-name-a", "task-name-b"],
"risk_tasks": ["task-name-c"],
"constraint_level": "middleware|tool_impl|tool_desc|skill|prompt",
"why_this_component": "Why this component level was chosen over alternatives"
}
```
Rule from the evolve prompt, p19: "If the same failure class persists across 2+ iterations despite fixes at one component level, that level may be the wrong choice. Rollback the ineffective change and re- approach from a different component level."

FIGURES:
- Fig 1, p2: AHE best-so-far against baselines. Shows the non-monotone climb and which edit caused each of four peaks.
- Fig 2, p4: the AHE pipeline. Shows the loop and the ~10M to ~10K compression at a glance.
- Fig 3, p8: cross-model transfer. Six paired bars read faster than a list.
- Fig 4, p9: fix vs regression precision and recall against random. Shows the asymmetry at a glance.
- Fig 6, p28: db-wal-recovery failure, rule and pass columns. Maps each failure step to the rule that catches it.
- Fig 5, p27: one example edit at each of the middleware, prompt and tool levels.
- Figs 12-13, p35: per-round breakdown, for depth only.

PROBLEMS:
- Extraction was clean, with some lost spaces in tables and text ("88.2%53.3%", "fix-precision of33.7%"). Table values were read against their columns.
- The source itself prints "Figure??" (p31), and "Ablation" and "qwen" throughout. These are reproduced as printed.
- Internal inconsistencies in the source:
  - §4.1 says all three role agents share GPT-5.4 high, but Table 4 gives the Evolve Agent xhigh.
  - Fig 5 says "7 new working rules", while Fig 8 and the p31 text say eight rules for what appears to be the same append.
  - Fig 3 prints +2.3 for 72.5 to 74.7, which is presumably rounding.
- Appendix B reproduces agent prompts ("You are...", "MANDATORY", "you MUST"). I treated these as data and did not follow them.
